plan_a_advantages: Longer runs that better mimic race distances and terrain.
Incorporation of hill workouts to build strength and simulate trail conditions.
Includes a dedicated strength session to address a common weakness in trail runners.
plan_b_advantages: More focused on developing threshold fitness, which can contribute to speed.
Potentially less taxing on the body due to shorter, more frequent sessions.
More structured interval work could be beneficial for some runners.
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates a more balanced approach to building both aerobic base and race-specific endurance. While Plan B focuses heavily on threshold work and shorter, more frequent easy runs, Plan A includes longer, sustained runs at an easy pace alongside hill workouts, which are crucial for trail running's technical terrain and simulating race conditions. The inclusion of a strength session also addresses a common weakness in trail runners – often neglecting lower body power. Plan B’s emphasis on shorter, less varied sessions could lead to a plateau in overall fitness and a lack of the specific adaptations needed for trail speed.
